Cache a module's plot step

Source: R/plot_tiers.R
cached_structure.Rd

Draws a module's plot (everything before apply_uniform_styling()) and keeps it in the session's cache, keyed on the data, the module's other reactive values the step reads (extra), and the inputs the step reads, so a styling change never redraws the plot and going back to settings already drawn (toggling an option back, Reset) re-uses the figure. The figure is built here (plotly::plotly_build()), so the styling step does not repeat that work.

Usage

cached_structure(build, input, session, data, params = NULL, extra = NULL)

Arguments

build

A function of isolate_fn that draws the plot and returns a list with at least fig. See the rules above.

input, session

The module's input and session.

data

The module's data reactive.

params

The reactive-defaults store from setup_reactive_defaults(), or NULL.

extra

A function of no arguments returning the module's other reactive values build reads (axis-limit and colour stores, the selection, ...), or NULL.

Value

A reactive returning build's value, with .build added: a number unique to each time the plot was drawn, kept with the value in the cache. The figure's layout.uirevision is set from it, so a styling change keeps the user's zoom while a different plot resets it.

Details

The inputs in the key are exactly those the step reads through the isolate_fn it is given: every isolate_fn(input$<key>) read is recorded, and the set only grows. So an input the step reads is always in the key (a stale plot otherwise), while inputs it never reads (the styling ones, widget bookkeeping, an input frozen by an update the step does not care about) are never in it. An entry stored before the set grew has a key of a different shape from every later one, so it can never be served for settings it was not drawn with.

On a miss the step is evaluated reactively, so it depends on what it reads in the usual way; on a hit the key's reads stand in for it. Errors are not cached. The key includes the module's namespace, so modules sharing a session never see each other's entries. Set options(VizModules.cache = FALSE) to turn caching off.

Three rules keep the cache honest

A step that breaks one of these does not fail: it draws a stale plot.

  • Read every input in the literal form isolate_fn(input$key). A wrapped read such as isolate_fn(as.numeric(input$size)) cannot be recognised, and a bare input$size bypasses isolate_fn altogether, so that input never reaches the key. Convert outside the call.

  • Name every other reactive the step reads in extra: colour and axis-limit stores, a debounced text input, a reactive argument. The exception is a reactive that only derives from data, which the key already covers.

  • Give it no side effects (notifications, reactiveVal() writes), since a cache hit skips them. Return anything else the module needs in the list instead.

See also

apply_uniform_styling() for the styling step, finalize_manual_edits() for sending a restyle as a layout-only update.

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Inside moduleServer(), with `params` from setup_reactive_defaults():
draw_myPlot <- function(isolate_fn) {
    p <- my_plot_fn(data(), x = isolate_fn(input$x.by), colors = palette_store())
    list(fig = plotly::ggplotly(p))
}
base_myPlot <- cached_structure(draw_myPlot, input, session, data,
    params = params, extra = function() list(palette_store())
)
generate_myPlot <- reactive({
    isolate_fn <- setup_auto_update_logic(input, params)
    apply_uniform_styling(base_myPlot()$fig, input, isolate_fn)
})
} # }
